skill.name: extension-email-calendar-events
skill.description: Organize calendar events in Motoko applications and send iCalendar invitations by email.
skill.summary: Add permission-controlled calendar event management and email invitations to Caffeine AI applications.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: All 24 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown links, code fences, module references, and ordinary Motoko uid identifiers. Semantic review found a medium-severity invitation abuse risk because public registration accepts unverified email addresses that are later included as event attendees.

remediation.issue: Public registration accepts an email address without proving that the caller controls it.
remediation.suggestion: Require email verification before activating a profile or adding its address to event attendees, and rate-limit registration and invitation delivery.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Email Enrollment Enables Unwanted Invitations
semantic_findings.description: Any caller can register an arbitrary unique email address without ownership verification. Registered addresses become event attendees and can later receive administrator-triggered invitations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example stores caller-supplied email addresses after only uniqueness checks, adds every stored profile to events, and provides an invitation-send operation.

content.value_statement: Building calendar workflows and iCalendar email delivery requires coordinated storage, permissions, and message formatting. This skill provides Motoko patterns for event management and invitation sending.
actual_capabilities: Defines Motoko interfaces for creating, updating, canceling, deleting, retrieving, and listing calendar events.
Shows how to add and remove attendees from stored events.
Generates UUID version 4 identifiers using a random seed.
Applies administrator permission checks to event management and invitation operations.
Builds attendee records from registered user profiles.
Sends iCalendar event invitations through the Caffeine AI email client.
limitations: Requires the Caffeine AI calendar events, authorization, and email packages.
Does not support receiving or processing attendee RSVP responses.
The example does not verify ownership of registered email addresses.
The example ignores the email delivery result and does not demonstrate retries.

use_cases.title: Add Scheduling to a Motoko Application
use_cases.description: Implement stored events, attendee management, and emailed iCalendar invitations in a Caffeine AI backend.

use_cases.title: Manage Internal Meeting Invitations
use_cases.description: Create an administrator-controlled workflow for scheduling meetings and inviting registered users.

use_cases.title: Review Calendar Integration Design
use_cases.description: Assess authorization, identity, event lifecycle, and email delivery patterns before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Calendar Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Add calendar event storage to my Motoko backend. Include create, get, list, update, cancel, and delete operations using the documented package.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs the core event lifecycle without email delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Add Permission-Controlled Invitations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an administrator-only flow that builds an event, adds selected verified attendees, and sends an iCalendar invitation through the email client.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs secure invitation delivery for selected users.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Existing User Profiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the calendar event example to my existing user profile model. Preserve authorization and require verified email ownership before adding attendees.
prompt_templates.scenario: An application already stores users and needs calendar integration.

prompt_templates.title: Harden the Full Event Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Motoko calendar workflow for authorization gaps, unverified recipients, invalid time ranges, duplicate sends, delivery failures, and event lifecycle errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team needs a deployment readiness review.

output_examples.input: Add a calendar event feature for administrator-managed team meetings.
output: A Motoko backend design with administrator-protected event operations.
Event records with unique identifiers, times, organizer details, and attendees.
An invitation flow using the Caffeine AI email client.

output_examples.input: Review my invitation workflow before deployment.
output: Verify each recipient email before adding it to an event.
Validate that the end time follows the start time.
Handle delivery failures and prevent accidental duplicate invitations.

output_examples.input: Explain the event lifecycle supported by this skill.
output_examples.output: Events can be created, retrieved, listed, updated, canceled, deleted, and sent to attendees as iCalendar email invitations.

best_practices: Verify email ownership before making a profile eligible for invitations.
Keep every event mutation and invitation operation behind explicit authorization checks.
Validate times, attendee addresses, delivery results, and duplicate-send conditions.
anti_patterns: Do not add every registered address to every event without selection or consent.
Do not ignore invitation delivery failures or assume that a send always succeeds.
Do not expose event mutation methods without role-based authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill add?
faq.answer: It provides Motoko patterns for calendar event storage, lifecycle operations, attendee management, and iCalendar email invitations.

faq.question: Which platforms does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Motoko backends built with Caffeine AI packages and works as guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can attendees send RSVP responses?
faq.answer: No. The documented component does not receive or process RSVP responses.

faq.question: Does it include authorization?
faq.answer: The example uses Caffeine AI authorization and restricts event administration and invitation sending to administrators.

faq.question: Which dependencies are required?
faq.answer: The workflow depends on the Caffeine AI calendar events, authorization, and email components.

faq.question: What should be added before production use?
faq.answer: Add email verification, input validation, selected attendee enrollment, delivery error handling, rate limits, and duplicate-send protection.
